Organisations, teams, projects, environments and blueprints — everything that is decided before anything is provisioned. Nothing on this server provisions anything; its two destructive tools remove records, never infrastructure.

| At a glance          |                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Endpoint**         | `https://g8deck.app/mcp/design`                                                                                          |
| **Server name**      | `g8deck-design`                                                                                                          |
| **Who can reach it** | Roles holding `mcp.access.design`. Of the customer roles, `user` holds it; `member` does not.                            |
| **Authentication**   | A personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer …`) or OAuth 2.1 sign-in — see [Connect an AI client](/docs/mcp/connect) |
| **Route limit**      | 60 requests per minute                                                                                                   |
| **Tools**            | 21 — 10 read, 9 write, 2 destroy                                                                                         |

Every tool needs a token carrying its tier: `mcp:read`, `mcp:write` or `mcp:destroy`, each tier including the ones before it. On top of the route limit, each caller gets 60 read, 20 write and 5 destroy calls a minute. Your role decides which tools answer at all; a tool you can see but lack the permission for answers `permission_denied` and names the permission. Secret and credential values never cross this boundary — tools take them inbound and report key names only.

## What the client is told

The server sends these instructions to every AI client that connects, before any tool is called. They are reproduced verbatim because they carry the reading rules that change what an answer means.

<details class="instructions">
<summary>Server instructions</summary>

```text
G8Deck blueprint server — design and check architecture before anything is provisioned.

Conventions:
- Call `whoami` first, then `list-organizations` / `list-projects` / `list-environments` to learn what you can address.
- `create-organization` makes one you own (capped per user by an administrator) and does not change your default; `invite-member` emails an invitation as member or administrator and needs you to own or administer that organisation. Membership starts only when the invitee accepts.
- `set-team-servers` decides which servers a team may deploy to (organisation owner/administrator only). A member of a team deploys only to its allocation — `create-deployment` and `clone-application` on the ops server refuse anything else, naming the team. Administrators are unaffected.
- `create-project` (in a team) and `create-environment` (in a project) are the New Project / New Environment pages' actions: a lead of the team or an organisation owner/administrator. Both are idempotent on the slug — an existing one is returned with `created: false`.
- Identify everything by uuid or slug. Every tool accepts an optional `organization`; the one actually used is echoed on every response.
- A blueprint is `Blueprint -> layers -> components`, with connections between layers. Layers carry a role (edge, lb, app, worker, db, cache, queue, storage, observability, identity) and replica bounds.
- **Catalogue blueprints (`is_system`) are read-only.** `clone-blueprint` copies one into your organisation so it can be edited.
- The component **catalogue** and the provisioner **registry** are different things. `list-component-types` reports both, and a component with `provisionable: false` will be refused at provision time — check before attaching it.
- `get-component-definition` returns not_found for an unregistered slug. That absence is the answer; do not infer an image or a port for it.
- `validate-blueprint` is the cheap check: layers with nothing attached, components with no provisioner, and layer roles no pipeline step consumes. The last is the dangerous one — such a layer provisions nothing and reports no error.
- `estimate-deployment` prices a blueprint against quota before a deployment exists. Node counts here are blueprint replicas; what each costs depends on the provider type.
- Nothing on this server provisions anything. Use the ops server (`/mcp/ops`) to create and run deployments.
- `move-project-to-organization` re-homes projects plus the infrastructure only they use in another organisation you also administer. Bookkeeping only — no machine is touched. `dry_run` defaults to true and lists every row and every refusal; the move is all or nothing.
- `delete-project` and `delete-environment` are the only destructive tools here, and neither touches infrastructure — they remove *records*. Both need `mcp:destroy` and both refuse while a live deployment still points at the record; tear the deployment down on the ops server first. Deleting a project takes its environments and its settled deployment records with it, because an environment whose project is gone is an orphan no page can show.
- **`delete-environment` confirms on the SLUG, not the name.** Environment names repeat — a whole fleet of them is called "Production" — so retyping a name would confirm nothing.
- Deletion here is a soft delete: rows leave every listing and can be restored by an operator with database access. Audit records are immutable and stay by design.
```

</details>

## Read tools

### `whoami`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code></p>

Report who you are: identity, roles, which MCP servers you may reach, your token's abilities, the organisations you can address and which one is used when you omit the `organization` argument. Call this first.

Takes no parameters.

### `list-organizations`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>organizations.view.list</code></p>

Organisations you are an active member of, and which one is used when you omit the organization argument.

Takes no parameters.

### `list-projects`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>projects.view.list</code></p>

Projects in an organisation, with the team each belongs to.

| Parameter      | Type    | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search`       | string  | Free-text search across name and slug.                            |
| `organization` | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |
| `page`         | integer | Page number, starting at 1.                                       |
| `per_page`     | integer | Results per page, 1-100 (default 20).                             |

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>environments.view.list</code></p>

Environments in an organisation, optionally narrowed to one project. Flags which are production-like, since promotion and approval rules key off that rather than off the name.

| Parameter      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project`      | string | Project uuid or slug.                                             |
| `organization` | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>blueprints.view.list</code></p>

Blueprints available to this organisation — the platform catalogue and any the organisation owns, flagged apart so a caller knows which it may edit.

| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search`       | string  | Free-text search across name and slug.                            |

| `organization` | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |
| `page`         | integer | Page number, starting at 1.                                       |
| `per_page`     | integer | Results per page, 1-100 (default 20).                             |

### `get-blueprint`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>blueprints.view.list</code></p>

One blueprint in full: layers with their roles and replica bounds, the components attached to each, the connections between them, and the topology graph the visualiser renders.

| Parameter                                     | Type   | Description                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blueprint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Blueprint uuid or slug.                                           |

### `validate-blueprint`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>blueprints.view.list</code></p>

Check a blueprint before anything is provisioned: layers with no components, component slugs no provisioner is registered for, and layer roles that no pipeline step consumes. A layer role nobody handles provisions nothing and reports no error, which is worse than an outright failure.

| Parameter                                     | Type   | Description                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blueprint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Blueprint uuid or slug.                                           |
| `organization`                                | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `estimate-deployment`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>deployments.view.list</code></p>

What a blueprint would cost before anything is created: node count from the layer replica bounds, the requested size, and the caller's remaining quota headroom. Answers "will this be refused" without creating a deployment to find out.

| Parameter                                     | Type   | Description                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blueprint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Blueprint uuid or slug.                                                      |
| `project`                                     | string | Project uuid or slug — include it to get quota headroom.                     |
| `size`                                        | string | Size to price (default small). One of: `small`, `medium`, `large`, `custom`. |
| `organization`                                | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.            |

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>component-registry.view.list</code></p>

The component registry — every component that can be attached to a blueprint layer, and whether a provisioner is actually registered for it. A catalogue entry with no provisioner is refused at provision time, so the two are reported together.

| Parameter            | Type    | Description                                                       |
| -------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `category`           | string  | Filter by component category.                                     |
| `search`             | string  | Free-text search across name and slug.                            |
| `provisionable_only` | boolean | Only components a provisioner is registered for.                  |
| `organization`       | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |
| `page`               | integer | Page number, starting at 1.                                       |
| `per_page`           | integer | Results per page, 1-200 (default 50).                             |

### `get-component-definition`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>component-registry.view.list</code></p>

What G8Deck will actually provision for a component slug: image, port, readiness probe and the command it runs. A slug that is not registered returns not_found — that absence IS the answer, and no image should be inferred for it.

| Parameter                                | Type   | Description                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slug` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Component slug, e.g. postgres, redis, minio (see list-component-types). |

## Write tools

### `create-organization`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>organizations.create.item</code></p>

Create an organisation you will own, initialised like the one given at sign-up: Starter plan and a first team led by you. Subject to the per-user ownership limit an administrator sets. Your default organisation is not changed — pass the returned uuid as `organization` to work in it.

| Parameter                                | Type   | Description                              |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Organisation name, unique across G8Deck. |
| `description`                            | string | Optional, up to 1,000 characters.        |

### `invite-member`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>organizations.manage.members</code></p>

Invite someone to an organisation by email, as a member or an administrator. They receive an email link valid for 7 days that works only for an account with that address. Requires being the owner or an administrator of the organisation. The invitation is audited.

| Parameter                                 | Type   | Description                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Email address to invite.                                                     |
| `role`                                    | string | member (default) or administrator. Ownership is never granted by invitation. |
| `organization`                            | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.            |

### `invite-members`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>organizations.manage.members</code></p>

Invite up to 200 people to an organisation by email in one call, all as members or all as administrators. Each address is answered separately: invited, or refused with the reason (not an email, already a member, already invited, members ceiling reached). A refusal stops nothing. Requires being the owner or an administrator of the organisation. Every invitation is audited.

| Parameter                                  | Type            | Description                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `emails` <span class="req">required</span> | array of string | Email addresses to invite, 1 to . Duplicates are collapsed.                                       |
| `role`                                     | string          | member (default) or administrator, for the whole batch. Ownership is never granted by invitation. |
| `organization`                             | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                 |

### `add-team-members`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>teams.manage.members</code></p>

Add people who are already in the organisation to one of its teams, all with one role (lead, member or viewer; default member). Identify each person by email or uuid. Someone unknown, outside the organisation or already on the team is skipped with a reason, never refused as a batch. Requires being a lead of the team or an owner/administrator of the organisation.

| Parameter                                 | Type            | Description                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `team` <span class="req">required</span>  | string          | Team uuid or slug, inside the organisation.                                                    |
| `users` <span class="req">required</span> | array of string | 1–50 people, each an email address or a user uuid. Each must already be in the organisation.   |
| `role`                                    | string          | Role for everyone added: lead, member (default) or viewer. One of: `lead`, `member`, `viewer`. |
| `organization`                            | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                              |

### `set-team-servers`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>teams.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Replace the set of servers a team may deploy to. Members of the team can then deploy only to these; organisation owners and administrators are unaffected. Pass an empty list to clear the allocation, after which members of that team cannot deploy at all. Each server must be a deployable infrastructure provider of the organisation, by uuid. Requires being an owner or administrator of the organisation. Nothing already deployed is touched.

| Parameter                                     | Type            | Description                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `team` <span class="req">required</span>      | string          | Team uuid or slug, inside the organisation.                                                                     |
| `providers` <span class="req">required</span> | array of string | Infrastructure provider uuids the team may deploy to. Replaces the current allocation; an empty list clears it. |
| `organization`                                | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                               |

### `create-project`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>projects.create.item</code></p>

Create a project in one of the organisation's teams — the same action and rules as the New Project page. Requires being a lead of that team or an owner/administrator of the organisation. The slug defaults to the name slugged. Idempotent: if the team already has a project with that slug, it is returned with created=false rather than a second one being made.

| Parameter                                | Type   | Description                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `team` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Team uuid or slug, inside the organisation.                                                     |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Project name, 2–120 characters.                                                                 |
| `slug`                                   | string | Letters, numbers, dashes and underscores. Defaults to the name slugged; unique within the team. |
| `description`                            | string | Optional, up to 1,000 characters.                                                               |
| `status`                                 | string | Default active. One of: `active`, `archived`, `locked`.                                         |
| `organization`                           | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                               |

### `move-project-to-organization`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>projects.move.organization</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Move one or more projects — with their environments, deployments and applications, and every server, database server, storage server, cache, file database, backup destination, integration and blueprint ONLY they use — to another organisation. Shared things never move: a blueprint a staying deployment uses is CLONED into the target; an integration something staying uses (e.g. the DigitalOcean account that also created other servers) stays, and the moving servers are re-pointed to the target organisation's own integration of the same provider (for a cloud-created server the dry run asks that integration whether it can see the machine, and refuses on a 404). Moved backup policies whose destination stays go to backup_destination, else the target default — never left writing into a destination of the source. include_servers brings extra servers along; left_behind lists source servers named like the projects that are NOT moving. Bookkeeping only: no machine is touched, and moving back reverses it. dry_run defaults to true and lists every row that would move and every reason it cannot; pass dry_run: false to apply. All or nothing: refused while shared infrastructure is still used by something staying behind (named), while a deployment is provisioning, destroying or scaling, when the target lacks its own integration, backup destination, git credential or GitHub App installation for a repository, when the target plan has no room, or unless you own or administer BOTH organisations. Audit history, invoices and usage records stay with the source.

| Parameter                                               | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projects` <span class="req">required</span>            | array of string | Project uuids or slugs in the source organisation. Move projects that share infrastructure together.                                                              |
| `target_organization` <span class="req">required</span> | string          | Organisation uuid or slug to move to. You must own or administer it.                                                                                              |
| `target_team` <span class="req">required</span>         | string          | Team uuid or slug in the target organisation that receives the projects.                                                                                          |
| `dry_run`                                               | boolean         | Default true: report what would move and why it cannot, changing nothing.                                                                                         |
| `backup_destination`                                    | string          | Uuid of a backup destination in the target (or one moving with the projects) for moved backup policies whose destination stays. Omit to use the target's default. |
| `include_servers`                                       | array of string | Uuids of extra servers in the source to move along — e.g. a storage machine listed under left_behind. Refused like any other server if something staying uses it. |
| `organization`                                          | string          | Source organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                          |

### `create-environment`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>environments.create.item</code></p>

Create an environment in a project — the same action and rules as the New Environment page. Requires being a lead of the project's team or an owner/administrator of the organisation. The slug defaults to the name slugged; is_production defaults to what the type implies (production and dr are production-like). Idempotent: if the project already has an environment with that slug, it is returned with created=false.

| Parameter                                   | Type    | Description                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Project uuid or slug.                                                                              |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span>    | string  | Environment name, 2–120 characters. Names repeat freely; the slug is what identifies it.           |
| `type` <span class="req">required</span>    | string  | One of: `local`, `development`, `staging`, `production`, `dr`, `preview`.                          |
| `slug`                                      | string  | Letters, numbers, dashes and underscores. Defaults to the name slugged; unique within the project. |
| `is_production`                             | boolean | Defaults to what the type implies.                                                                 |
| `description`                               | string  | Optional, up to 1,000 characters.                                                                  |
| `organization`                              | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                  |

### `clone-blueprint`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>blueprints.clone.system</code></p>

Copy a blueprint into this organisation so it can be edited. Catalogue blueprints are read-only; cloning is how a tenant makes one its own.

| Parameter                                     | Type   | Description                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blueprint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Blueprint uuid or slug to clone.                                  |
| `name`                                        | string | Name for the clone. Defaults to the source name plus "(clone)".   |
| `organization`                                | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

## Destructive tools

Each needs a token carrying `mcp:destroy`, and most also need an identifying value retyped into a confirmation argument. A mismatch is refused and audited.

### `delete-project`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>projects.delete.item</code></p>

Delete a project, together with its environments and the records of deployments already torn down. Refused while any deployment is still live — destroy those first. Requires the project name retyped exactly in confirm_name, and a token carrying mcp:destroy. Both the deletion and any refused attempt are audited.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `project` <span class="req">required</span>      | string | Project uuid or slug.                                                    |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The project's exact name, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.        |

### `delete-environment`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>environments.delete.item</code></p>

Delete one environment. Refused while any deployment in it is still live. Confirmation here is the environment SLUG, not its name: environment names repeat across projects — a whole fleet of them is called "Production" — so retyping the name would confirm nothing. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy, and is audited either way.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `environment` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Environment uuid or slug.                                                                                                  |
| `confirm_slug` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The environment's exact SLUG, retyped — not its name, which repeats across projects. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                          |
